articles.title: Are Socialists Actually Leaving Wokeness Behind?
articles.content:
本周，编辑Peter Suderman、Katherine Mangu-Ward、Nick Gillespie和Matt Welch讨论了众议员Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez承认“Woke 1是疯狂的”，以及民主党社会主义者协会（DSA）将焦点转向经济实惠是否代表了与2020年政治的真正决裂。他们争论进步派是否真的从疫情时期的过激做法中脱离出来，DSA的经济议程是否更可行，以及为何经济实惠成为左翼的有力信息。

编辑们还探讨了生活成本如何引发右翼内部的争斗，从网上关于20美元卷饼的争论到更大的分歧，包括关税、移民和伊朗战争。他们讨论了唐纳德·特朗普最近试图结束出生公民权的努力，以及剑桥大学Jason Arday抄袭丑闻对学术界持续的意识形态问题的启示。最后，一位听众询问巨额CEO薪酬和大规模裁员是否削弱了资本主义的理由。

33:12——听众对资本主义的提问

articles.summary:
This week, editors Peter Suderman, Katherine Mangu-Ward, Nick Gillespie, and Matt Welch discuss Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez's admission that "Woke 1 was crazy" and whether the Democratic Socialists of America's (DSA) new focus on affordability represents a genuine break from the politics of 2020. They debate whether progressives have actually moved on from the excesses of the pandemic era, whether the DSA's economic agenda is any more workable, and why affordability has become such a potent message on the left.

The editors also examine how the cost of living is driving infighting on the right, from the online battle over $20 burritos to the larger splits over tariffs, immigration, and the Iran war. They discuss President Donald Trump's latest attempt to end birthright citizenship and what the Jason Arday plagiarism scandal at Cambridge University says about academia's lingering ideological problems. Finally, a listener asks whether enormous CEO pay packages and widespread layoffs undermine the case for capitalism.

 

0:00—Ocasio-Cortez says "Woke 1 was crazy"

15:19—Conservatives debate the cost of burritos

28:49—Trump's birthright citizenship order

33:12—Listener question on capitalism

46:08—Arday scandal and resignation

55:54—Weekly cultural recommendations

articles.title: Reminder: Second Annual Aspiring Free Speech Scholars Workshop
articles.content:
由桑德拉·戴·奥康纳法学院（ASU）与胡佛研究所（斯坦福大学）联合主办的第二届"自由言论学术新锐研讨会"

由于技术问题，任何在2026年6月4日之前提交的稿件均已丢失；请重新提交（或首次提交）至以下新链接：https://tinyurl.com/aspiring-free-speech-scholars

如果你是法律学生、司法书记员、律师或初步学术研究者，希望发表关于自由言论法的期刊文章，并希望从领先的自由言论专家那里获得建议，那么请在2026年8月16日星期日之前提交你的草稿。（仍应为草稿，而非已经发表或预计在六个月内发表的文章。）无需担心文章草稿是否完全抛光，甚至某些部分是否不完整；我们审阅的是草稿，而非成品。

我们计划选择我们认为特别有前途的提交，并邀请其作者参加研讨会，在研讨会上他们可以展示论文并获得有益的反馈。研讨会将于2026年10月24日星期六（前一晚提供晚餐）在亚利桑那州凤凰城的桑德拉·戴·奥康纳法学院举行。我们将于2026年9月8日星期二通知被选中的作者。

我们有资金支付被选中作者的交通和住宿费用。参与资格限于目前发表不超过三篇法律相关期刊文章的人员。

我们还计划从审阅的文章中正式认定并表彰0至3篇最佳文章。如果作者愿意，他们的文章也可被考虑发表在《自由言论法杂志》（http://JournalOfFreeSpeechLaw.org），通常是在根据研讨会反馈修改文章后。

如果感兴趣，请将你的草稿提交至http://tinyurl.com/aspiring-free-speech-scholars（需Google账号登录）。请单行间距，并格式化文章，以便我们更容易阅读。

请不要在文档或文件名中包含你的姓名或法学院隶属关系，也请不要包含作者致谢你的导师和其他人的声明。请将文件名设置为你的文章标题（或标题的可识别子集）。我们希望在不了解作者身份的情况下审阅文章草稿。

如有问题，请查看http://tinyurl.com/aspiring-free-speech-faq；如果问题未被解答，请发送邮件至volokh@stanford.edu。

特别感谢斯坦顿基金会的慷慨支持。

* * *

詹姆斯·温斯坦，桑德拉·戴·奥康纳法学院，亚利桑那州立大学，丹·克拉奇奥洛宪法法学讲座教授
尤金·沃洛克，胡佛研究所（斯坦福大学）托马斯·M·西贝尔高级研究员，加州大学洛杉矶分校法学院加里·T·施瓦茨杰出法学教授（荣休）

原文来自Reason.com：提醒：第二届自由言论学术新锐研讨会
articles.summary:
Second Annual Aspiring Free Speech Scholars Workshop
jointly sponsored by the Sandra Day O'Connor College of Law (ASU)
and the Hoover Institution (Stanford University)

Because of a technical problem, any submissions before June 4, 2026 were lost; please resubmit (or submit for the first time) at the new URL listed below, https://tinyurl.com/aspiring-free-speech-scholars

Are you a law student, judicial law clerk, lawyer, or beginning academic hoping to publish a journal article on free speech law? Would you like the opportunity to get advice about your draft from leading free speech scholars?

If so, send us your draft by Sunday, August 16, 2026. (This should still be a draft article, not an article that's already published or expected to be published within six months.) Don't worry if the article draft isn't fully polished, or even if some portions are incomplete; we're reviewing drafts, not finished products.

We plan to select the submissions that we think are particularly promising, and invite their authors to a workshop where they can present their papers and get helpful feedback on them. The workshop will be Saturday, October 24, 2026 (with dinner the night before) at the Sandra Day O'Connor College of Law in Phoenix. We will inform the selected authors by Tuesday, September 8, 2026.

We have funds to pay for transportation and lodging for the selected authors' trips. Eligibility is limited to people who have so far published three or fewer law-related journal articles.

We also plan to officially recognize zero to three of the top articles among those we review. If the authors wish, they can also have their articles reviewed for publication in the Journal of Free Speech Law (http://JournalOfFreeSpeechLaw.org), presumably after they revise the articles in light of the workshop feedback.

If you're interested, please submit your draft at http://tinyurl.com/aspiring-free-speech-scholars (Google logon required). Please single-space, and format the article nicely, so we can more easily read it.

Please do not include your name or law school affiliation in the document or document filename, and please do not include an author's note thanking your advisors and others. Please make your filename be the title of your article (or some recognizable subset of the article title). We want to review the article drafts without knowing the authors' identities.

If you have questions, please check http://tinyurl.com/aspiring-free-speech-faq; if your question isn't answered there, please e-mail volokh@stanford.edu.

Many thanks to the Stanton Foundation for its generous support.

* * *

James Weinstein, Dan Cracchiolo Chair in Constitutional Law and Professor of Law, Sandra Day O'Connor College of Law, Arizona State University

Eugene Volokh, Thomas M. Siebel Senior Fellow, Hoover Institution (Stanford University), and Gary T. Schwartz Distinguished Professor of Law Emeritus, UCLA School of Law

The post Reminder: Second Annual Aspiring Free Speech Scholars Workshop appeared first on Reason.com.

articles.title: Don't Let AOC Retcon Her Starring Role in 'Woke 1'
articles.content:
纽约州民主党众议员亚历山德リア·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯(Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez)在周日关于她曾经对文化左翼立场的热情态度上出现了惊人的转变，引发了公众的关注。她说：“有一位本地市议员有一句名言——‘觉醒1.0是疯狂的’。”她笑称。她指的是纽约市议员奇·奥塞(Chi Ossé)在推特上的类似表述，试图解释他之前为什么说下一任市议会议长“不应当是白人男性”。

这种态度过于漫不经心。尽管令人鼓舞的是许多进步派人士已经放弃了一些（但绝非全部）非常糟糕的主张，但任何人都不应天真地轻易接受这些转变。此外，他们试图让“觉醒1.0”看起来像是一场突如其来的灾难——就像飓风或地震——而他们被动地接受，因为除此之外别无选择，这完全是在转移视线。

实际上，AOC和奥塞听起来有点像《新闻播报员》中的朗·伯爵(Ron Burgundy)在一场充满暴力和血腥的战斗后说“那发展得太快了”，同时还悠闲地啜饮着啤酒。虽然“觉醒1.0”可能没有像史蒂夫·卡瑞尔用三叉戟杀死某人的场景那样荒谬，但那仍然是一个相当疯狂的时代，而AOC等政治人物不仅没有试图阻止这一切，反而积极参与其中。

2019年，AOC发布了一段视频，批评想在社区花园种植花菜而非木薯的纽约市民是“殖民主义的同谋”。（花菜和木薯都不是纽约土生植物。）2022年，她介入了关于性别中立词“拉丁裔人”的争论，批评其他民主党人过早放弃包容性的尝试，尽管民调一致显示大量拉丁裔人并不喜欢这个词，并且更不愿意投票支持使用该词的民主党人。五个月前，她还认为马可·鲁比奥(Marco Rubio)声称牛仔文化源于西班牙是“有失偏颇”的，AOC认为“非裔奴隶人民”才是这一贡献的创造者。

这些只是AOC主动参与“觉醒”讨论并支持更荒谬立场的一些例子。

关于“觉醒”过度的争论确实涉及对“觉醒”定义的不同理解。在过去十年中（甚至更早），人们通常将其称为“政治正确”，主要关注与言论文化监管相关的烦恼：美德宣示、安全空间与微侵犯的概念，以及取消文化。但由于“政治正确”拗口，而“觉醒”只有一个音节——更适合标题！——后者最终取而代之。此外，“觉醒”也与远左政策立场联系在一起，这些立场并不完全与文化和言论相关，例如废除警察、边境以及美国政府的各种准民主机构（参议院、最高法院、选举人团等）。其中，警察问题特别成为“觉醒”过度的标志之一，乔治·弗洛伊德的死亡引发了对过度执法的反弹，但这种反弹走得过远，主要成为远左活动家进行思想监管的借口，而职业骗子则趁机发财。

可以公正地认为，文化潮流已经反转，左翼媒体人士、活动学生和社交媒体暴民已经失去了强制执行正统观念并惩罚异见者的能力。民主党政治家普遍认为他们不愿挑战这些势力是他们如今失去权力的原因之一。

然而，就像荷马在克里斯托弗·诺兰的《奥德修斯》中描述自己的时代为“青铜时代”一样，将其称为“觉醒1.0”并说这一切都结束了，并承诺永不重蹈覆辙，多少有些过于超现实。AOC对“觉醒”的新态度至多是一种极其软弱的选择，一旦文化潮流再次转向，她显然会毫不犹豫地放弃这个立场。
articles.summary:
Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D–N.Y.) raised eyebrows this weekend when she merely shrugged off her previous enthusiasm for electorally toxic far-left cultural positions.

"I have a local city councilman who has this saying: 'Woke 1 was crazy,'" said AOC with a laugh. She was referencing a tweet by Chi Ossé, a New York City councilman, who similarly uttered this line in an attempt to explain why he had previously said a "white man should not be the next speaker" of the City Council.

Simply put, this attitude is far too blasé. While it's encouraging that so many progressives have backed away from some (though by no means all) of their really terrible ideas, no one should be so naive as to accept these conversions at face value. Moreover, it's quite deflective of them to act as if "Woke 1" was something bad that just sort of happened—like a hurricane or an earthquake—and they passively accepted it because what else could they do?

In fact, AOC and Ossé sound a bit like Anchorman's Ron Burgundy issuing his well-quoted lamentation about his team's outrageously violent, murder-fueled battle royale—"that escalated quickly"—while nonchalantly sipping a beer. Perhaps Woke 1 involved nothing quite so absurd as Steve Carell killing a guy with a trident, but it was still a fairly crazy time, and importantly, political figures such as AOC did absolutely nothing to try to stop it. She was more than complicit in it.

In 2019, AOC posted a video criticizing New Yorkers who wanted to grow cauliflower instead of yuca in their community gardens as complicit in colonization. (Neither cauliflower nor yuca is indigenous to New York.) In 2022, she weighed in on the fight over the gender neutral term Latinx, taking fellow Democrats to task for being too quick to abandon their attempts at inclusivity, despite polls consistently showing that large shares of Latin people did not like the term very much and would be less likely to vote for Democrats who used it. And she said that it was offensive for Secretary of State Marco Rubio to claim cowboy culture originated in Spain; AOC instead credited "African enslaved peoples" with this contribution. That was five months ago.

Those are just a few colorful examples of AOC willfully participating in wokeness discourse and militating in favor of the more ridiculous position.

It's true that broader debates about the excesses of wokeness inevitably involve competing definitions of what counts as woke. In the previous decade (and prior), people tended to label this thing political correctness and mainly focused on irritation at speech-related cultural policing: virtue signaling, the concepts of safe spaces and microaggressions, and cancel culture. But since political correctness is clunky and woke is just a single syllable—much better for headlines!—the latter eventually won out. Wokeness also became associated with far-left policy positions that are not strictly related to culture and speech, such as abolishing the police, borders, and various quasi-democratic aspects of the U.S. government (the Senate, the Supreme Court, the Electoral College, and so on). The policing issue in particular has become one of the defining aspects of woke overreach, as the killing of George Floyd sparked a backlash against excessive policing that went way too far and mostly became a pretext for far-left activists to do some thought policing of their own while professional grifters enriched themselves.

It's certainly fair to conclude that the cultural pendulum has swung back the other way, and note that left-wing media figures, activist students, and social media mobs no longer have nearly as much power to enforce orthodoxy and punish dissenters. Democratic politicians largely attribute their reticence to challenge such forces as one of the reasons they are now thoroughly out of power.

But much like Odysseus referring to his own time period as "our Age of Bronze" in Christoper Nolan's very successful (though not universally appreciated) adaptation, there's something a bit too meta about calling it "Woke 1" and saying, well, that's all over now, and we'd never do it again. Trust us.

At best, AOC's newfound ambivalence for wokeness is a profoundly weak choice, and one that she would clearly eagerly jettison if the pendulum swung back in that direction.

The post Don't Let AOC Retcon Her Starring Role in 'Woke 1' appeared first on Reason.com.

articles.title: Trump Teased a Deal To Open Hormuz 'Tomorrow.' It's Been a Week.
articles.content:
上周，特朗普政府暗示与伊朗就重新开放因战争关闭的荷尔木兹海峡达成协议。特朗普总统8月4日表示，这项协议“可能在明天或后天达成”。财政部长斯科特·贝森特当天也表示，“我们可能今天或明天就能达成协议，重新开放海峡并朝着更正常的状态迈进。”然而，现在是8月10日，协议仍遥遥无期。

伊朗最高国家安全委员会秘书周六宣称，只有在永久结束战争、结束美国对伊朗的封锁和金融制裁，以及获得经济赔偿的情况下，才会允许荷尔木兹海峡重新开放。（前两项也是双方6月签署的和平备忘录的一部分，第三项是新要求。）特朗普周日对Axios表示，他现在仅“半主动”地与伊朗进行谈判，认为这种状况会“自行解决”。

在此期间，海峡的局势与过去几个月没有变化。伊朗坚称有权通过伊朗控制的航道引导船只，并对不服从的船只开火。美国则引导油轮通过阿曼水域的航道，并关闭了船只的无线电转发器。市场研究服务商Commodity Context表示，上周五的原油运输量约为500万桶，低于战争前的每日2000万桶。另一家数据公司Kpler报告称，周末只有32艘船通过海峡，其中17艘使用了伊朗航道。

Commodity Context创始人罗里·约翰逊( Rory Johnson)表示，即使是目前水平的美国支持的“黑暗过境”也“无法持续”，因为进入波斯湾的空油轮不足。

2月28日，美国和以色列对伊朗进行了突然袭击，据其设计者称，这场战争将在几天或几周内迫使伊朗屈服。然而，事实并非如此。伊朗政府很快发现，它有机会通过控制世界经济来惩罚攻击它的国家，从商人那里勒索赎金，并最终在和平协议中争取到更多让步。原本预计能够重塑中东、符合华盛顿利益的战争，反而变成了一场试图回到战前状态的斗争。

特朗普既无法忍受军事解决方案，也无法接受外交解决方案。他曾多次威胁要对伊朗进行极端升级，但每次都在被部下告知美国军队弹药不足后退缩——最近一次是在上周。特朗普虽然在纸面上达成了美国和伊朗均可接受的和平协议，但由于美国国内政治的限制，无法贯彻执行。任何让步，即使对美国没有成本，也会遭到情绪化的强烈反对。

4月的停火协议承诺结束整个地区的战争，包括以色列在南黎巴嫩的军事行动。面对以色列的反对，特朗普迅速试图改变协议，将黎巴嫩排除在外。6月的备忘录承诺结束黎巴嫩的战争并解冻伊朗国外的银行账户。再次面对国内攻击关于“支付”伊朗的说法时，特朗普没有跟进。每次，伊朗领导人都会回到谈判桌前，要求更多的前期让步，同时加剧对荷尔木兹海峡航运的骚扰。

上周，伊朗和阿曼达成协议，共同管理荷尔木兹海峡。两国将设立一个通过伊朗水域的单一入境车道和一个通过阿曼水域的单一出境车道，使两国都能对交通实行否决权。特朗普政府据称愿意支持伊朗-阿曼的外交努力，但伊朗外交部长阿巴斯·阿拉奇(Abbas Araghchi)随后宣称，荷尔木兹海峡不会在没有美国前期让步的情况下开放。

针对伊朗增加的赔偿要求，特朗普周一宣布，他“也要求伊朗赔偿”。他重申了引发战争的数十年的怨恨清单。特朗普的一些怨恨是真实的，比如伊朗支持伊拉克的游击队和镇压本国人民。但他也指责伊朗支持2000年对美国“科尔”号驱逐舰的袭击，而这一袭击是由“基地”组织发动的，该组织是伊朗的死敌。这一抱怨指向了许多鹰派最初对战争的希望：伊朗应该为美国在中东的失败买单，并恢复美国在该地区的荣誉。

然而，军事力量无法在承诺的时间和成本内迫使伊朗做出这种投降。现在特朗普的胜利理论，正如他在Axios中所阐述的那样，是持续的美国封锁将使已经遭受战争摧残的伊朗分崩离析。当然，敌人也有发言权。特朗普上月重新实施封锁后，也门胡塞武装开始直接袭击沙特油田。周一，美国战略石油储备降至40年来的最低水平。

有一些乐观的理由：双方都意识到这是一场“向下竞赛”。伊朗总统马苏德·佩泽什基安(Masoud Pezeshkian)周六表示：“愿上帝保佑，我们将到达一个点，摆脱这个非战非和的状态。”特朗普上周对支持者表示：“我宁愿达成协议，因为我不想杀人。”如果他能在发动战争之前就有这样的认知就好了。
articles.summary:
Last week, the Trump administration teased a deal with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz closed by war. President Donald Trump said on August 4 that the deal "could happen tomorrow or the next day." Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent said the same day that "we may have a deal today or tomorrow to open the strait and move towards a more normalized position." It is now August 10, and no deal is in sight.

Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary declared on Saturday that it would only allow the Strait of Hormuz to reopen with a permanent end to the war, an end to the U.S. blockade and financial sanctions on Iran, and financial compensation. (The first two points were also part of the June peace memorandum that both countries signed, and the third is a new demand.) Trump told Axios on Sunday that he is now "only semi-negotiating" with Iran and that the situation will just "work out" on its own.

Meanwhile, the situation in the strait itself is the same as it's been for the past few months. Iran is insisting that it has the right to route shipping through an Iranian-controlled corridor and is shooting at ships that don't comply. The U.S. is guiding convoys of oil tankers, with their radio transponders turned off, through a corridor in Omani waters. Oil flows were at around 5 million barrels on Friday, down from 20 million barrels per day before the war, according to the market research service Commodity Context. Kpler, another data firm, reports only 32 ships transited the strait over the weekend, 17 of which used the Iranian corridor.

Rory Johnson, founder of Commodity Context, wrote that even the current level of U.S.-backed "dark transits" is "unsustainable," simply because not enough empty tankers are entering the Persian Gulf.

The U.S.-Israel surprise attack on February 28 was supposed to bring Iran to heel within a matter of days or weeks, according to its architects. Instead, it created a whole new headache. The Iranian government quickly discovered that it had an opportunity to throttle the world economy in order to punish the countries attacking it, extract ransom from merchants, and, eventually, to leverage more concessions out of a peace deal. A war that was supposed to reshape the Middle East in Washington's favor instead became a struggle to get back to the status quo ante.

Trump has been unable to stomach either the military or the diplomatic solution. He has threatened Iran with extreme escalation, only to back down multiple times—most recently last week—after being told by his generals that they simply do not have enough ammunition to protect U.S. troops. Trump has been able to strike peace deals acceptable to the U.S. and Iran on paper, but without being able to follow through, largely because of domestic U.S. politics. Any concession, even those that cost Americans nothing, runs into emotionally charged opposition.

The April ceasefire agreement had promised an end to the war across the entire region, including Israel's campaign in southern Lebanon. Faced with Israeli pushback, Trump quickly attempted to change the deal to exclude Lebanon. The June memorandum promised both an end to the war in Lebanon and the unfreezing of Iranian bank accounts abroad. Again, faced with domestic attacks about "paying" Iran money, Trump didn't follow through. Each time, Iranian leaders have come back to the table demanding more concessions up front while escalating their own harassment of Hormuz shipping.

Last week, Iran and Oman struck a deal between themselves to manage the Strait of Hormuz. Rather than having separate Iran-backed and U.S.-backed routes, the two countries would have a single inbound lane through Iranian waters and a single outbound lane through Omani waters, giving both countries a veto over traffic. The Trump administration was reportedly willing to support the Iranian-Omani diplomacy, but Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi then declared that Hormuz would not open without U.S. concessions up front.

In response to Iran's added demand for compensation, Trump declared on Monday that he is "likewise demanding compensation from Iran." He recited the decades-old list of grievances that had motivated the push for war in the first place. Some of Trump's grievances, such as Iranian support for guerrillas in Iraq and the government's repression of its own people, are real. But he also blamed Iran for the 2000 attack on the USS Cole by Al Qaeda, a sworn enemy of Iran. That complaint points to many hawks' original hope for the war: Iran was supposed to pay for U.S. failures across the Middle East and restore American honor in the region.

But military force simply wasn't able to force that kind of Iranian surrender, at least not on the promised timeline at the promised cost. Now Trump's theory of victory, as he articulated it to Axios, is that the ongoing U.S. blockade will cause the already war-damaged Iran to fall apart. Of course, the enemy gets a vote, too. A few days after Trump reimposed the blockade last month, Iran's Houthi allies in Yemen began directly attacking Saudi oil infrastructure. The U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve, which has blunted much of the impact of the war so far, fell to its lowest level in four decades on Monday.

There is some reason for optimism: Both sides realize they're in a race to the bottom. "God willing, we will reach a point where we can get out of this state of neither war nor peace," Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Saturday. "I'd rather make a deal because I don't want to kill people," Trump told supporters last week. If only he had come to this insight before starting the war.

The post Trump Teased a Deal To Open Hormuz 'Tomorrow.' It's Been a Week. appeared first on Reason.com.

articles.title: Suspending College Student for Saying Man Who Insulted Her "Needa Get Blasted" + Having Posted Shooting Range Video (Year Before) Violated First Amendment
articles.content:
2024年9月5日，林莫伊（HGTC护理学校学生）在校外通过Snapchat群组发送了一条消息，该群组包含一些HGTC学生。消息内容涉及其男友室友的校外互动，该室友既非HGTC学生也非员工。林莫伊写道："但算了，我原本想友善一点，但某个长相奇怪穿面包服的陌生男人骂我是婊子，他需要被好好收拾一下。"……
2024年9月11日，林莫伊在与学校官员会面时否认"收拾"一词指代身体伤害，并解释道她的意思是该室友应被指出责或承担行为后果。林莫伊还表示她和父母均不持有枪支。被告称林莫伊的陈述表明她与枪支无关。原告否认这一描述，并称她并未声称自己从未开过枪、无枪支经验或与持枪人士无关联。法庭记录显示，在9月11日会议结束时，HGTC接受了林莫伊对Snapchat评论的解释。9月20日的行为决定书后来记载称，林莫伊被告知当时没有证据证明她违反学生守则，且学院接受了她对Snapchat评论的解释。原告进一步称，索耶内部沟通曾表示"没有针对他人的直接威胁"，巴特和索耶在与学生交谈后也达成一致结论。被告称该事件仍在审查中，HGTC需继续评估安全和干扰问题。……

2024年9月13日，HGTC发现林莫伊一年前在Instagram上发布的一段视频，视频中林莫伊身着西部风格服装向靶子开枪。原告称该视频是在她入学前拍摄的，地点在私人场地，与HGTC无关，未提及任何HGTC学生、员工或校园。被告称该视频使他们质疑林莫伊对Snapchat消息的解释及其与枪支的关系。巴特请求佛尔授权实施临时停学。佛尔批准了。原告称，在批准临时停学前，佛尔已获悉Snapchat消息和Instagram视频。被告称佛尔基于安全问题作出了合理决定。

2024年9月17日，林莫伊再次与HGTC人员（包括巴特和索耶）会面，讨论Instagram视频。林莫伊承认视频中人是她，称视频拍摄于2023年感恩节前后，枪支非她所有，且仅此一次开枪。她还表示可允许HGTC检查其物品，HGTC拒绝了。会议中，林莫伊收到临时停学和禁止入校通知……

2024年9月20日，HGTC发布行为决定书，对林莫伊实施停学并禁止入校。决定书列出两项纪律基础：使用"收拾"一词的Snapchat消息和林莫伊开枪的Instagram视频。决定书称，Instagram视频使HGTC质疑林莫伊对"收拾"一词的解释，并在"当今氛围"下，林莫伊"未披露视频"并使用"收拾"一词引发了对其能否留在护理专业的担忧。决定书还称，两项事实造成"相关枪支存在和使用的严重不安"，影响了学习环境，因为学生和员工表示感到不安全。9月20日的决定认定林莫伊违反了学生守则，禁止干扰教育过程、他人权利或正常校园功能的条款。……

法院认为林莫伊的言论受第一修正案保护，因此对其有利判决：
该Snapchat消息是在校外发送的。消息出现在一个包含HGTC学生的私人Snapchat群组中，但并非学校主办活动，不涉及课程内容，未提及HGTC人员，也未提到任何HGTC校园或活动。消息涉及林莫伊男友室友的校外互动，该室友既非HGTC学生也非员工。林莫伊写道该室友"需要被好好收拾一下。"

该短语粗俗、愤怒，若字面理解或脱离语境可能引起担忧。但第一修正案不允许公立学院将每个激进或模糊的短语视为不受保护的言论。语境很重要。该消息并非针对室友或HGTC，未指定任何HGTC学生、员工、教室或校园为目标。当巴特和索耶于9月11日采访林莫伊时，林莫伊否认"收拾"指代身体伤害，解释称该室友应被指出责或承担行为后果。9月20日的行为决定书承认HGTC已接受林莫伊的解释，并告知她当时没有证据表明她违反学生守则。……

Instagram视频同属校外表达。视频发布大约一年前被HGTC发现，显示林莫伊身着西部风格服装向靶子开枪。记录未显示该视频在HGTC场地拍摄、涉及HGTC活动、提及HGTC或针对任何HGTC学生或员工。被告称Instagram视频改变了Snapchat消息的语境，因为林莫伊此前表示她和父母不持有枪支。因此被告认为该视频使他们质疑林莫伊对Snapchat消息的解释及其与枪支的更广关系。该论点解释了HGTC为何继续调查，但并未独立证明Instagram视频本身不受保护。合法靶击，仅此而已，并非威胁。仅存在之前视频展示合法使用枪支的情况，并不会将另一条模糊的Snapchat消息转变为表达犯罪暴力的严重意图。Instagram视频可以作为HGTC回应的背景环境，包括其调查和任何临时安全措施的合理性。但该视频本身是校外表达，未针对HGTC或任何社区成员，不在第一修正案保护范围之外。……

被告还声称林莫伊的言论构成真实威胁。真实威胁不受第一修正案保护。但真实威胁例外仅限于表达犯罪暴力意图针对特定个人或群体的严重陈述。……

在最有利于被告的记录下，Snapchat消息使用的语言可能引起担忧。"收拾"一词可能带有暴力意味，当学生或教职员报告该语言使他们感到不安或不安全时，HGTC官员有权调查。学校无需忽视潜在安全问题，尤其是当报告的陈述似乎涉及暴力时。但调查与纪律不同。记录未显示林莫伊传达了针对HGTC学生、员工或校园的犯罪暴力的严重意图。Snapchat消息涉及非学生的校外个人纠纷，未威胁HGTC，未指定校园目标，且未发送给消息中提及的人。在询问时，林莫伊否认任何暴力含义，解释称该人应被指出责或承担后果。HGTC的9月20日决定承认这一解释最初被接受。Instagram视频并未改变这一结论。视频显示林莫伊大约一年前向靶子开枪。它不包含威胁语言，未提及Snapchat消息，未指定任何HGTC相关目标。模糊的俚语短语和旧的靶击视频的结合可能证明了进一步调查的正当性，但并未将林莫伊的言论转变为真实威胁。记录也未证明Counterman诉科罗拉多州案所要求的心理状态（鲁莽）因素。证据未显示林莫伊有意忽视Snapchat消息可能被理解为对HGTC学生或员工犯罪暴力的严重威胁的实质风险。她的解释、校外语境、非学生消息对象和HGTC最初接受她的解释都证明该陈述并非真实威胁。因此，被告未证明真实威胁学说将林莫伊的言论排除在第一修正案保护范围之外……

剩余问题在于HGTC是否可以因林莫伊的校外言论实质且重大地干扰了学校运作（依据Tinker诉Des Moines独立学区）或HGTC合理预见到这种干扰而对其进行纪律处分。法院承认HGTC对学生安全的合法利益及维持一个安全的教育环境的合法利益，使得HGTC有权调查Snapchat消息、与学生和教职员交谈、采访林莫伊、审查Instagram视频并采取合理措施评估是否存在真实威胁或干扰。但Tinker要求不仅仅是不适、忧虑或普遍安全问题。公立学校不得基于未分化的恐惧或避免不快来限制受保护的言论。根据Mahanoy地区学区诉B.L.，HGTC的监管利益因言论发生在校外、在私人社交媒体环境下、与非学生和非校园事务相关而减弱。判决摘要记录未显示实际实质性干扰。记录反映一些学生或员工在获悉Snapchat消息和Instagram视频后表达不适或安全问题。但记录未显示课程停止、教学实质性改变、校园运作受到重大中断或林莫伊在校内参与干扰他人权利的行为。……

HGTC也没有识别足够事实支持合理预见实质性干扰。合理预见必须基于证据，而非猜测。9月20日的决定称，在"当今氛围"下，Snapchat消息和Instagram视频引发了对枪支的忧虑，使学生和员工感到不安全。法院不否认这些担忧。但宪法问题不是HGTC官员是否被允许担忧或调查。问题在于记录是否包含足够事实表明林莫伊的校外言论导致或合理威胁HGTC教育环境的实质性干扰。根据记录，并非如此。本案事实与针对学生或学校人员的威胁、严重骚扰、有针对性的欺凌、学校主办言论或言论以可预见方式实质性侵入学校环境的案件实质不同。林莫伊的Snapchat消息涉及非学生和校外个人事务。Instagram视频很旧，涉及靶击，未提及HGTC。记录不支持认定两项内容单独或共同给HGTC提供了足够的宪法依据来实施停学和禁止入校令……

因此，法院认为林莫伊的Snapchat消息和Instagram视频是受保护的言论。被告有权调查报告的担忧并采取合理措施确定是否存在威胁或实质性干扰。但第一修正案不允许HGTC在未有真实威胁、实际实质性干扰或记录支持的合理预见实质性干扰的情况下，因受保护的校外表达而对林莫伊进行纪律处分……

法院在预审禁令阶段已作出相似结论；我曾在2024年12月讨论过这一点。

但是法院拒绝了Lemoine关于学校行为剥夺她正当程序的单独主张。本·勒克莱尔克（Ben LeClercq）和大卫·戴尔·阿什利（David Dale Ashley）代表Lemoine出庭。这篇名为《因称侮辱她的人“需要被轰炸”及一年前发布射击场视频而暂停大学生学籍，侵犯了第一修正案》的文章最初出现在Reason.com。
articles.summary:
Some excerpts from today's long opinion by Judge Joseph Dawson, III (D.S.C.) in Lemoine v. Horry Georgetown Tech. Coll.:

On September 5, 2024, while off campus, Lemoine [a cosmetology student at HGTC] sent a message in a Snapchat group that included some HGTC students. The message concerned an off-campus interaction involving Lemoine's boyfriend's roommate, who was not an HGTC student or employee. Lemoine wrote: "But naw I was trying to be nice but f[**]k that some random ugly ass in bread looking f[**]k dude called me a bitch he needa get blasted." [Expurgation in the court decision. -EV] …

[In a meeting with school officials on September 11, 2024,] Lemoine denied that "blasted" referred to physical harm and explained that she meant the roommate should be called out or held accountable for his behavior. Lemoine also stated that neither she nor her parents owned guns.

Defendants contend that Lemoine's statements suggested a broader disassociation from firearms. Plaintiff disputes that characterization and contends she did not state that she had never fired a gun, had no experience with guns, or had no association with anyone who possessed firearms.

The record reflects that, at the conclusion of the September 11 meeting, HGTC accepted Lemoine's explanation of the Snapchat comment. The September 20 conduct decision later recounted that Lemoine had been told there was then no evidence to find her in violation of the Student Code and that the College had accepted her explanation for the Snapchat comment. Plaintiff further contends that Sawyer communicated internally that there had been "no direct threat to others," and that Batten and Sawyer reached the same conclusion after speaking with students. Defendants contend the matter remained under review and that HGTC was required to continue assessing safety and disruption concerns….

On September 13, 2024, HGTC discovered a video posted to Lemoine's Instagram account about a year earlier, in which Lemoine fired a handgun at a target while wearing western-style attire. Plaintiff contends the video predated her enrollment at HGTC, was taken on private property, did not involve HGTC, and did not refer to any HGTC student, employee, or campus. Defendants contend the video caused them to question Lemoine's prior explanation of the Snapchat message and her statements concerning firearms.

Batten requested authorization from Fore for an interim suspension. Fore authorized the interim suspension. Plaintiff contends that, before authorizing the interim suspension, Fore was presented with both the Snapchat message and the Instagram video. Defendants contend Fore acted reasonably based on the safety concerns presented to her.

On September 17, 2024, Lemoine again met with HGTC personnel, including Batten and Sawyer, to discuss the Instagram video. Lemoine acknowledged that she was the person in the video, stated that the video was from around Thanksgiving 2023, stated that the gun did not belong to her, and stated that it was the only time she had fired a gun. She also offered consent for HGTC to search her belongings, which HGTC declined. At that meeting, Lemoine received an interim suspension and no-trespass notice….

On September 20, 2024, HGTC issued a conduct decision suspending Lemoine from HGTC and imposing a no-trespass order. The decision identified two matters as the basis for discipline: the Snapchat message using the term "blasted" and the Instagram video of Lemoine firing a handgun. The decision stated that the Instagram video caused HGTC to question Lemoine's explanation of the term "blasted," and that, "[i]n today's climate," Lemoine's "failure to disclose the existence of the video" together with her use of "blasted" caused concern about her ability to remain in the cosmetology cohort. The letter further stated that the two facts caused "a significant amount of apprehension related to the presence and use of guns" and had impacted the learning environment because students and employees expressed that they felt unsafe.

The September 20 decision concluded that Lemoine violated the Student Code provision prohibiting conduct that disrupts the educational process, interferes with the rights of others, or adversely interferes with normal college functions and services….

The court concluded that Lemoine's speech was protected by the First Amendment, and thus granted Lemoine summary judgment on that issue:

The Snapchat message was sent while Lemoine was off campus. The message appeared in a private Snapchat group that included some HGTC students, but it did not arise from school-sponsored activity, did not involve coursework, did not address HGTC personnel, and did not refer to any HGTC campus or event. The message concerned an off-campus interaction involving Lemoine's boyfriend's roommate, who was neither an HGTC student nor an employee. Lemoine wrote that the roommate "needa get blasted."

The phrase was crude, angry, and capable of causing concern if read literally or in isolation. But the First Amendment does not permit a public college to treat every intemperate or ambiguous phrase as unprotected speech. Context matters. The message was not directed to the roommate or to HGTC, and did not identify any HGTC student, employee, classroom, or campus as a target. When Batten and Sawyer interviewed Lemoine on September 11, Lemoine denied that "blasted" referred to physical harm and explained that she meant the roommate should be called out or held accountable for his behavior. The September 20 conduct decision letter acknowledged that HGTC had accepted Lemoine's explanation and had told her there was then no evidence to find her in violation of the Student Code. …

The Instagram video likewise involved expression outside the school setting. The video was posted about a year before HGTC discovered it. It showed Lemoine firing a handgun at a target while wearing western-style attire. The record does not show that the video was recorded on HGTC property, involved HGTC activity, referred to HGTC, or was directed toward any HGTC student or employee.

Defendants argue that the Instagram video changed the context of the Snapchat message because Lemoine had previously stated that she and her parents did not own guns. Defendants therefore contend that the video caused them to question Lemoine's explanation of the Snapchat message and her broader relationship to firearms.

That argument explains why HGTC continued its investigation. It does not, standing alone, establish that the Instagram video itself was unprotected speech. Lawful target shooting, without more, is not a threat. Nor does the mere existence of a prior video depicting lawful firearm use transform a separate ambiguous Snapchat message into a serious expression of intent to commit unlawful violence.

The Instagram video may be considered as part of the surrounding context for HGTC's response, including the reasonableness of its investigation and any temporary safety measures. But the video itself was off-campus expression, not directed at HGTC or any member of the HGTC community, and not inherently outside the protection of the First Amendment….

Defendants also contend that Lemoine's words and actions constituted a true threat. A true threat is not protected by the First Amendment. But the true-threat exception is limited to serious expressions of intent to commit unlawful violence against a particular individual or group of individuals….

Viewing the record in the light most favorable to Defendants, the Snapchat message used language that could cause concern. The term "blasted" can carry violent connotations, and HGTC officials were entitled to investigate when students or faculty reported that the language made them uncomfortable or unsafe. Schools are not required to ignore potential safety concerns, particularly when a reported statement appears to reference violence.

But investigation is different from discipline. The record does not show that Lemoine communicated a serious expression of intent to commit unlawful violence against an HGTC student, employee, or campus. The Snapchat message referred to a nonstudent involved in an off-campus personal dispute. It did not threaten HGTC, did not identify a school target, and was not sent to the person referenced in the message. When questioned, Lemoine denied any violent meaning and explained that she meant the person should be called out or held accountable. HGTC's own September 20 decision acknowledged that this explanation had initially been accepted.

The Instagram video does not change that conclusion. The video showed Lemoine firing a handgun at a target about a year earlier. It did not contain threatening language, reference the Snapchat message, or identify any HGTC-related target. The combination of an ambiguous slang phrase and an old target-shooting video may have justified additional inquiry, but it did not transform Lemoine's speech into a true threat on this record.

Nor does the record establish the mental-state component [recklessness] required by Counterman v. Colorado. The evidence does not show that Lemoine consciously disregarded a substantial risk that her Snapchat message would be understood as a serious threat of unlawful violence toward HGTC students or employees. Her explanation, the off-campus context, the nonstudent subject of the message, and HGTC's initial acceptance of her explanation all weigh against treating the statement as a true threat. Accordingly, Defendants have not shown that the true-threat doctrine removed Lemoine's speech from First Amendment protection…..

The remaining question is whether HGTC could discipline Lemoine's off-campus speech because it materially and substantially disrupted school operations [under Tinker v. Des Moines Indep. School Dist.] or because HGTC reasonably forecast such disruption. The Court recognizes that HGTC had a legitimate interest in student safety and in maintaining an educational environment in which students and employees could attend class without reasonable fear of violence. That interest permitted HGTC to investigate the Snapchat message, speak with students and faculty, interview Lemoine, review the Instagram video, and take reasonable steps to assess whether a genuine threat or disruption existed.

But Tinker requires more than discomfort, apprehension, or generalized safety concerns. A public school may not restrict protected speech based on undifferentiated fear or a desire to avoid unpleasantness. And under Mahanoy Area School Dist. v. B.L., HGTC's regulatory interest was diminished because the speech occurred off campus, outside school supervision, in a private social-media setting, and concerned a nonstudent and non-school matter.

The summary-judgment record does not show actual substantial disruption. The record reflects that some students or employees expressed discomfort or safety concerns after learning of the Snapchat message and Instagram video. But the record does not show that classes stopped, instruction materially changed, campus operations were substantially interrupted, or Lemoine engaged in conduct at school that interfered with the rights of others….

Nor did HGTC identify facts sufficient to support a reasonable forecast of substantial disruption. A reasonable forecast must be grounded in evidence, not speculation.

The September 20 decision stated that, "[i]n today's climate," the Snapchat message and Instagram video caused apprehension related to guns and caused students and employees to feel unsafe. The Court does not minimize those concerns. But the constitutional question is not whether HGTC officials were permitted to be concerned or to investigate. The question is whether the record contains sufficient facts showing that Lemoine's off-campus speech either caused or reasonably threatened a material and substantial disruption of HGTC's educational environment. On this record, it does not.

The facts here are materially different from cases involving threats directed at students or school personnel, severe harassment, targeted bullying, school-sponsored speech, or speech that foreseeably invades the school environment in a substantial way. Lemoine's Snapchat message concerned a nonstudent and off-campus personal matter. The Instagram video was old, involved target shooting, and did not reference HGTC.

The record does not support a finding that either item, separately or together, gave HGTC a constitutionally sufficient basis to impose a suspension and no-trespass order….

Accordingly, the Court concludes that Lemoine's Snapchat message and Instagram video were protected speech. Defendants were entitled to investigate the reported concerns and to take reasonable steps to determine whether a threat or substantial disruption existed. But the First Amendment did not permit HGTC to discipline Lemoine for protected off-campus expression absent a true threat, actual substantial disruption, or a reasonable forecast of substantial disruption supported by the record….

The court had reached a similar result at the preliminary injunction stage; I blogged about that in December 2024. But the court rejected Lemoine's separate claim that the school's actions denied her due process.

Ben LeClercq and David Dale Ashley (LeClercq Law Firm) represent Lemoine.
